description: Our team consists of young explorers who want to combine technical skills with storytelling to provide a simple solution for complex problems
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a free digital storybook and quiz game about six machines humans left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space: Luna 9, the Apollo Lunar Module, Voyager 1, Mars 3, Pioneer 10 and Opportunity. Each page has an illustration, a kid-friendly story, quick facts, a “Where is it now?” box, a word to know, a surprising fact and a Listen button that reads the page aloud. A companion quiz lets young readers answer a question for each world to “restore” its museum. It answers the challenge by introducing school-age space fans to the hardware left across the solar system and the science it made possible. It matters because these machines are more than leftovers. They carry messages to the stars, NASA still studies them, and their stories can inspire the next generation of explorers.
details:
What it does. The storybook has 9 pages, one machine per page. Pages share a layout but change colour by place: violet for the Moon, red-orange for Mars, teal for deep space. Readers move through it with Next/Back buttons, page dots, arrow keys, swipe on phones or a direct link to any page. The quiz site has a home page with “How to play” and the stories, plus one quiz page each for the Moon, Mars and deep space. A right answer turns green and a wrong one turns red, so a wrong answer is a prompt to read again.

Benefits and impact. It makes space history approachable for ages 5–12 with short sentences, defined vocabulary and read-aloud support. It also teaches honest science. Where something is unconfirmed (Luna 9’s exact location, Mars 3’s fate, the Apollo 11 top stage), the book says “not confirmed” instead of guessing. The goal is for young readers to see old spacecraft as part of ongoing exploration.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript only. The illustrations are inline SVG. The Listen button uses the browser’s Web Speech API, and page links use the URL hash. Fonts are Atkinson Hyperlegible, Bricolage Grotesque, JetBrains Mono and Kranky.

Creativity. The “museum” framing, the Orbit & Bloom idea (“old spacecraft, blooming into new stories”) and a timeline of 60 years of machines.

Factors we considered. Accuracy, with facts checked against NASA JPL, NASA Science and other named sources. Readability (large type, plain language). Accessibility (keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support). Working on phones and tablets.
